findings.title: Retain shutdown evidence and finish private-file cleanup when the transient unit is collected
findings.trigger: Owned transient PG unit stops successfully and is garbage-collected before the subsequent systemctl show, or is already collected when cleanup begins.
findings.actualBehavior: stopPgService calls serviceState without allowMissing after the successful stop. The documented not-found/code1 response throws before recorded PID/scope checks, private environment/password removal and pg-cleanup receipt. The separate initial not-found branch returns complete:true,unitNeverStarted:true even when a ready pg-service receipt exists, without PID/scope checks or normal-shutdown proof.
findings.impact: A valid successful shutdown can fail the diagnostic and leave the full private PG environment file behind; the already-collected branch can instead misclassify a known started service as never started. No file was actually created or uploaded by this review.
findings.requiredCorrection: Preserve independently qualified final exit/result evidence before unit state can be unloaded, or retain a valid unit reference through the needed readback. A missing unit may establish unit absence, not successful normal PG exit. Verify recorded process and scope retirement in both branches, classify missing result honestly as unknown/unqualified, and guarantee removal or explicitly excluded retention of owned private files on error while retaining the original failure. Merely setting allowMissing cannot reconstruct lost Result metadata.

findings.title: Own spawned collectors and attach exit/error handlers before awaiting startup work
findings.trigger: A collector has spawned but its birth read fails or startup aborts before launchCollector returns; output.close also creates an await before error/close listeners are registered.
findings.actualBehavior: startResourceCapture only pushes a collector into state.children after awaited launchCollector returns. Birth-read EACCES leaves the already spawned handle unregistered. finishResourceCapture cleans only state.children, so its finally path never retires that child. There are zero error handlers during the first post-spawn await, so an early spawn error can also escape the intended exit promise.
findings.impact: A failed serving smoke can leave an external proc/SQL observer alive outside the cleanup owner and contaminate later quiet windows until its deadline or external cleanup. Existing pure partial-startup test exercises only validateCleanupUnit predicates and does not cover this acquisition path.
findings.requiredCorrection: Attach error/close handlers synchronously with child creation before the first await, register every spawned handle immediately with the acquisition owner, and ensure partial-start failure performs finite identity-safe teardown/join even when birth capture never succeeds. Preserve the startup error and cleanup uncertainty; an empty children list is not proof that no process was started.

primaryDocumentation.title: systemd-run: RemainAfterExit and transient-unit collection
primaryDocumentation.supports: RemainAfterExit retains a completed service until it is explicitly stopped; successful transient units are normally unloaded.

primaryDocumentation.title: systemd.unit: Unit Garbage Collection
primaryDocumentation.supports: Unused inactive units may be unloaded and execution results, exit codes/signals and resource statistics are lost except logs.
